data.body:
OPERATOR-ATTESTED — (1) THE v2 ARMS ARE PROVIDER-CLEAN, and (2) THE DECISION TAKEN.

(1) PROVIDER-CLEAN PROOF. `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` was set for both slot runs and the per-call model
tallied by parsing each JSONL row and keeping rows that carry BOTH a `model` field and a
non-null `input_tokens` (`provider_parity.usage_model_tally`). This is the corrected technique:
the plan said to grep for lines carrying `model=` and `input_tokens=`, but the sink is JSONL
written as `json.dumps(row)` with JSON KEYS, so a `model=` grep matches nothing. `run_slot`
executes arm v1 to completion then arm v2, so the log is ordered and every row from the first
`bedrock:` row onward belongs to the v2 arm.

  standard slot   v1 arm  84 case-runs  {anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6: 84}
                  v2 arm  84 case-runs  {bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6: 84}
                  v2 NON-BEDROCK CALLS: {}   <- zero
  frontier slot   v1 arm  84 case-runs  {anthropic:claude-opus-4-8: 84}
                  v2 arm  84 case-runs  {bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8: 84}
                  v2 NON-BEDROCK CALLS: {}   <- zero

  84 rather than 90 rows per arm is the two container fixture cases x 3 epochs, which raised
  before any model call; outcome was "ok" on all 84 rows of all four arms. So the split-brain
  this ticket's earlier comments warned about (a bare `claude-*` ladder rung silently routing a
  "Bedrock" arm to direct Anthropic) did NOT occur: not one call on either v2 arm resolved to a
  non-Bedrock provider.

  The mechanism that guarantees it is now pinned by a test rather than only observed. Items run
  concurrently, and each worker executes under a context COPIED inside the `gate_config` +
  `gate_read_root` scopes; a bare thread inherits neither ContextVar. Mutation-verified: remove
  the copy and every worker on BOTH arms resolves the ambient `claude-opus-4-8` instead of its
  arm's model — the split-brain, reproduced on demand.

(2) THE DECISION. Bedrock FAILS the parity bar at BOTH class slots (standard: 1 decision flip;
frontier: 2 flips, agreement 0.929 < 0.95, and the false-accept criterion). The bar requires
zero decision-level flips and it is not met, so:

  DO NOT claim Bedrock as a first-class provider on the strength of this run, and DO NOT let S8
  (eb6e) cut the production review bot over to Bedrock citing a cleared parity bar. There is no
  cleared parity bar to cite.

  REMEDIATE, do not reinterpret. Three specific things stand between this evidence and a
  defensible pass, and none of them is "Bedrock is worse":
  a. 635f (missing `errored` guard at `parity.py:107`) should land first. It did not affect THIS
     run — error rate is 0.000 on all four arms and every flipped pair is errored=False on both
     sides — but it must be fixed before anyone re-runs on a flakier day, because a single
     throttle would fabricate a flip and produce a spurious Bedrock failure.
  b. The false-accept criterion appears INVERTED (`parity._recall_false_accept` returns the
     fraction of clean items correctly NOT blocked — specificity — and `parity_report` fails the
     run when it RISES). The frontier slot is failed by it for false-firing LESS than direct
     Anthropic. Until that is settled, that particular failure should not be read as evidence
     against Bedrock. Filed as a separate ticket.
  c. "Zero decision flips" may itself be an unattainable bar for a paired LLM run at N=3 on a
     28-item gold set, independent of provider: all three flips here are single-item majority
     changes on FP-style cases, and the same corpus re-run against direct Anthropic on BOTH arms
     has not been measured. THAT is the missing control. Recommended next step before any
     re-litigation of Bedrock: run the harness Anthropic-vs-Anthropic to establish the bar's
     own noise floor. If a same-provider run also produces flips, the bar needs a tolerance and
     that is a change to the bar, decided deliberately — not something S6 should smuggle in.

  What this run DOES establish positively, and S8 may rely on: both Bedrock inference-profile
  ids are invokable in 896586841071/us-east-1; structured output over Converse is 100% valid on
  360 case-runs across both model classes; the runtime error rate is zero; latency is at or
  better than direct Anthropic (standard 9.9% faster, frontier within 0.1%), which retires the
  N=1 pilot's "~35% slower" hint; the `supports_temperature: False` override for opus-4-8 works
  in practice (zero sampling-parameter rejections in 90 frontier v2 case-runs); and provider
  routing is clean. The unmet part is specifically the decision-agreement criterion.
